description: Golden-vector corpus for .epr-meta evaluator parity — the governance correspondence theorem. Every evaluator (Python PreToolUse hook, Python git-gate, Rust eprfs-meta/epr-cli, any future Codex-side gate) MUST derive these exact outcomes from these cascades. Two runtimes deriving different verdicts from the same manifests is a forked governance plane. Source of truth: this file; runners project it into temp fixture trees. Decision vocabulary: epr:schema:enum:decision (permit|refuse|refer). Severity law: deny > ask > inject; measure/dispatch never block. Ceiling law: ask-class outcomes are REFER (first-class, routed), never a collapsed warn.

vectors.name: no-rule-clean-allow
vectors.law: Silence when no rule fired is clean; nothing to witness.

vectors.name: deny-fires-refuse

manifests..epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: no-new-md
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Deny-class refusal on the deterministic floor.

vectors.name: ask-fires-refer

manifests.notes/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: confirm-notes
    class: ask
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Ask IS the ceiling marker at authoring time — a routed referral, never a collapsed warn and never conflated with deny.

vectors.name: deny-beats-ask-severity

manifests..epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: root-deny
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test
manifests.sub/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: sub-ask
    class: ask
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Severity single-winner: deny > ask. Cascade merges root-first; both fire; deny wins.

vectors.name: inject-only-permits-with-advice

manifests.adv/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: advise-only
    class: inject
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Inject narrows nothing — permit carrying advisory witness.

vectors.name: measure-never-blocks

manifests.m/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: observe-md
    class: measure
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    measure:
      kind: level
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Observation tier: fires, is witnessed, never blocks.

vectors.name: measure-without-kind-is-malformed

manifests.mk/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: observe-md-no-kind
    class: measure
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: A measure rule MUST declare measure.kind (level|rate|ratio) — an undeclared kind is how a rate gets compared to a cumulative level (L6, landed 2026-08-11 in 8da9b519c). A rule-integrity failure routes rather than guessing. ADDED 2026-08-12 to pin a MEASURED divergence: the previous form of `measure-never-blocks` carried no kind, and the two evaluators split on it — Python refused the manifest as malformed while Rust accepted it and applied the rule. That is a forked governance plane by this corpus's own definition, and it survived because no gate runs either runner. This vector is expected to PASS in Python and FAIL in Rust until eprfs-meta enforces L6; it is the corpus-level half of the `governance-plane-single-evaluator` habit.

vectors.name: dispatch-permits-and-directs

manifests.d/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: dispatch-review
    class: dispatch
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    parameters: { dispatch-agent: code-reviewer, dispatch-prompt: "review the governance registry edit" }
    why: test

vectors.law: Dispatch never blocks; it witnesses and directs a background agent. A silently-dropped dispatch verdict is a defect (pre-slice behavior).

vectors.name: unresolvable-validator-refers

manifests.v/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: ghost-validator
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    validator: epr:validator-does-not-exist
    why: test

vectors.law: An unresolvable reference must never soften to inject (the pre-slice soundness inversion) and must not hard-deny at authoring polarity: it routes. Declared runtime-scoped validators (e.g. rust-only) are NOT unresolvable — they are Unavailable-by-declaration and skip without downgrading the rule.

vectors.name: unresolvable-validator-on-inject-does-not-harden

manifests.iv/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: advisory-ghost
    class: inject
    when: { write: "*.rs", new: true }
    validator: epr:validator-does-not-exist
    why: test

vectors.law: The soundness inversion has TWO directions and `unresolvable-validator-refers` only pins one. An unresolvable ref must not SOFTEN a rule declared to gate (that vector, class: deny) — and it must not HARDEN one declared advisory. A `class: inject` rule's own text says it never blocks; escalating it to a routed `ask` stops the agent and waits on a human for a rule whose author declared it non-blocking, costing agency instead of buying safety. The verdict is CLAMPED TO THE DECLARED CLASS: route only what was already meant to gate. ADDED 2026-08-12 pinning a MEASURED divergence — Python clamps (permit/inject), Rust returns Ask unconditionally (refer). It survived because the only unresolvable-validator vector used `class: deny`, where the two agree by coincidence of severity.

vectors.name: runtime-scoped-validator-skips-clean

manifests.rs/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: scoped-elsewhere
    class: inject
    when: { write: "*.rs", new: true }
    validator: epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality
    why: test

vectors.law: A validator DECLARED to belong to another runtime is Unavailable-by-declaration, not unresolvable: it skips clean and never downgrades the rule. This is the honest asymmetry a two-host plane is allowed to have — but only when BOTH hosts can tell a declared absence from an unknown one. ADDED 2026-08-12 pinning the other half of the same measured divergence: Python carries `RUNTIME_SCOPED_VALIDATORS` and skips, Rust's provider falls through `_ => Unavailable` and cannot distinguish 'not mine to run' from 'never heard of it', so three Python-owned validators route to judgment there. `epr:validator-dna-hash-neutrality` is the discriminator (Python-owned, live in elohim/holochain/dna/.epr-meta). The fix is a SHARED registry both hosts bind — not a second implementation of each validator, which would double the plane rather than collapse it.

vectors.name: malformed-manifest-refers

manifests.bad/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: broken
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md" }
    unknown-predicate-key: true

vectors.law: Rule-integrity failure is a ceiling event: the gate cannot know what governance intended, so it routes rather than guessing — unless the write TARGETS the manifest itself (fixing is never blocked).

vectors.name: sovereignty-guard-fires-advisory

manifests.sg/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: sovereignty-ontology-guard
    class: dispatch
    when: { write: "*.md" }
    validator: epr:validator-sovereignty-ontology-guard
    parameters: { dispatch-agent: storyteller, dispatch-prompt: "review only the net-new framing" }
    why: test

vectors.law: A values guard reads its vocabulary from a content-addressed frame atom (elohim/sdk/schemas/v1/frames/, seeded into every fixture) and classifies net-new apex framing with no declared frame as abstain. The verdict is advisory: it inherits the rule's declared class (dispatch), so it witnesses and directs the storyteller sidecar but never asks or denies (ruling R-C1; Python's `Verdict(None, …)` passthrough mirrors `ValidatorOutcome::Classified`, R-C7). This vector alone cannot go red on an unreadable atom: `Unavailable` clamps to the same declared dispatch class and permits, witnesses and directs exactly as a classification does. Its discriminating half is `sovereignty-guard-silent-on-declared-frame`.

vectors.name: ownership-guard-fires-advisory

manifests.og/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: ownership-ontology-guard
    class: dispatch
    when: { write: "*.md" }
    validator: epr:validator-ownership-ontology-guard
    parameters: { dispatch-agent: storyteller, dispatch-prompt: "review only the net-new framing" }
    why: test

vectors.law: The ownership sibling of `sovereignty-guard-fires-advisory`: the same frame-atom read, the same advisory inheritance of the declared dispatch class. Both hosts must agree that a classified frame verdict permits, witnesses and directs — never asks. This vector alone cannot go red on an unreadable atom: `Unavailable` clamps to the same declared dispatch class and permits, witnesses and directs exactly as a classification does. Its discriminating half is `ownership-guard-silent-on-declared-frame`.

vectors.name: sovereignty-guard-silent-on-declared-frame

manifests.sd/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: sovereignty-ontology-guard
    class: dispatch
    when: { write: "*.md" }
    validator: epr:validator-sovereignty-ontology-guard
    parameters: { dispatch-agent: storyteller, dispatch-prompt: "review only the net-new framing" }
    why: test

write.content:
sovereignty-frame: bounded
Members hold a self-sovereign identity within the commons.

vectors.law: The discriminating half of `sovereignty-guard-fires-advisory`. A declared legitimate frame is silent, and only a guard that READ its atom can know that: an unreadable atom is `Unavailable`, which the evaluator clamps to the rule's declared class and witnesses. So a fires-vector alone passes whether or not the classifier ran; this vector goes red the moment a host cannot read the frame atoms it was seeded with.

vectors.name: ownership-guard-silent-on-declared-frame

manifests.od/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: ownership-ontology-guard
    class: dispatch
    when: { write: "*.md" }
    validator: epr:validator-ownership-ontology-guard
    parameters: { dispatch-agent: storyteller, dispatch-prompt: "review only the net-new framing" }
    why: test

write.content:
stewardship-frame: inalienable
A person holds true ownership of her own image.

vectors.law: The ownership sibling of `sovereignty-guard-silent-on-declared-frame`: a declared stewardship frame (here the inalienable frame) is silent only when the host read the ownership atom.

vectors.name: sovereignty-guard-v5-homoglyph-fires-without-prefilter
vectors.law: Review M2, ruling R-C13. The guard rows bind by policy ref, and @5 carries no raw `contains-any` pre-filter: @4's case-sensitive `["sovereign", "Sovereign"]` substring test ran before the validator, so a homoglyph (U+2011 hyphen, Cyrillic о) never reached the NFKC + confusable fold and the guard was blind to it live. Both runners seed the live policy registry into the fixture, so this vector exercises the row as the registry declares it: the validator scopes itself over the folded shadow and classifies. Pair: `ownership-guard-v5-caps-fires-without-prefilter`.

vectors.name: ownership-guard-v5-caps-fires-without-prefilter

write.content: SELF-SOVEREIGN identity is the promise. Own your data.

vectors.law: The ownership sibling of `sovereignty-guard-v5-homoglyph-fires-without-prefilter`. @4's pre-filter was `["ownership", "Ownership"]`, so `own your data` — a phrase in the ownership atom — never fired unless the word `ownership` also appeared. @5 drops it and the lowercased shadow matches.
